messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: People with MS who supplemented with vitamin D had significantly reduced depression risk (PHQ-2 positive screen).
Sentence: "Participants who supplemented with omega 3s, particularly flaxseed oil, had frequent fish consumption, supplemented with vitamin D, meditated, and had moderate alcohol consumption had significantly reduced depression risk."
Measured as: depression risk (PHQ-2 score ≥3)
Population: People with multiple sclerosis recruited internationally via Web 2.0 platforms
Intervention: Self-reported vitamin D supplementation
Comparator: Participants not supplementing with vitamin D
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 2,459
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: 25OHD levels did not differ significantly between patients treated for depression and healthy controls.
Sentence: "The level of 25OHD and 1,25(OH)2D3 did not differ significantly between the examined groups."
Measured as: depression (patients treated for depression vs healthy controls)
Population: 99 patients aged 46.9 ± 11 years treated for depression and 45 healthy subjects
Intervention: Not applicable (observational; serum 25OHD measured)
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 144
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A links self-reported vitamin D supplementation to lower PHQ-2 depression risk in people with MS, while Study B finds no difference in serum 25OHD between treated depressed patients and healthy controls, so the findings point different ways and the populations differ most.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"population","also_differs":["intervention","outcome_measure","design_or_bias"],"detail":"population: MS patients (PHQ-2 screen) vs treated depression patients and healthy controls; exposure: self-reported supplementation vs serum 25OHD level"}
